set.prevailing_wage_basis: 2026 Supportive Housing NOFA Section 2.23 and Exhibit 4.03.01 (OC Housing and Community Development, March 6, 2026): projects funded only with local resources such as MHSA/BHSA may be exempt from Davis-Bacon; use of MHSA funds 'may require' state prevailing wage under Labor Code 1720, the County may require the applicant's legal counsel to confirm whether state prevailing wage applies, and an applicant may submit an attorney opinion that it does not (Section 4.03.01). Davis-Bacon applies separately when HOME (12+ HOME units) or PBVs (9+ units) are layered. State prevailing wage therefore depends on Labor Code 1720(b) and 1720(c) project facts.
set.layering_notes: Orange County's BHSA program is the deepest county PSH source in the 13 counties researched: $18,400,000 a year in planned capital plus a COSR that replaces PBVs when none are available (zero interest, forgivable over 15 to 20 years, sized to cover MHSA unit operating deficits). Pair the capital with 4% credits and OCHA or city PBVs; use COSR when PBVs are refused. MHSA/BHSA capital alone may avoid Davis-Bacon; the NOFA says state prevailing wage may apply under Labor Code 1720 and is decided per project with counsel input, while HOME (12+ units) or PBVs (9+ units) trigger Davis-Bacon. Terms are in Attachment D of the 2026 NOFA (opened); budget figures from the Integrated Plan PDF on ochealthinfo.com (opened). HCA does not run its own developer NOFA.
set.audit_note: Tier 4 spot check November 8, 2026: Attachment D loan limits ($207,235 capital plus $207,235 COSR per regulated unit), 30% AMI targeting, 49% cap, CES referral and COSR terms match; Integrated Plan (June 11, 2026 version) confirms $73,500,000 Housing Interventions, $18,375,000 plus $990,508 capital, $14,000,000 rental subsidies, $6,787,829 operating subsidies, $36,750,000 chronically homeless, 6 projects with 56 BHSA units of 416, 476 completed and 196 pipeline units, 2,396 goal and $5.50 leverage. NOFA page still lists the 2026 NOFA as open (exhibits updated October 2026); funds first-come, first-served until committed or replaced. The $20,500,000 Housing Finance Trust grant was not found in the Integrated Plan and was not rechecked. Attachment D says units are encouraged (not required) to be at least 450 square feet and one-bedroom.

reason: Material: prevailing_wage_trigger was true, but the 2026 NOFA says MHSA/BHSA-only projects may be exempt from Davis-Bacon and state prevailing wage may apply under Labor Code 1720 subject to counsel review, so it is unclear; award, AMI, cycle and deadline match.

set.typical_award_size: Requirement and entitlement, not a subsidy. Sec. 18.52.020.010 adopts Government Code 65915 density bonuses and incentives by reference; Sec. 18.52.020.020 requires affordable housing to be provided under Chapter 17.40 (Inclusionary Housing); Sec. 18.52.020.030 makes review by right (Gov. Code 65583.2(h) and (i)) on Sixth Cycle Housing Element candidate sites for low and very low income units when at least 20% of units are restricted to lower income households; Sec. 18.52.020.040 allows affordable housing on institution-owned property per Sec. 18.38.023. Sec. 18.52.030 implements Housing Crisis Act replacement housing (55-year rental and 45-year ownership restrictions, relocation and right of first refusal; the right of first refusal does not apply to 100% lower income projects). Chapter 17.40 (Ord. 6593, October 29, 2024) requires rental projects of 35 or more units to set aside at least 10% of units onsite (at least 7% low income and 3% very low income) for 55 years, with in-lieu fee, offsite and land dedication alternatives; ownership projects are exempt.
set.affordability_requirement: State density bonus thresholds (5% very low, 10% low, 10% moderate for-sale, 100% affordable) with 55-year rental covenants; by-right review requires 20% lower income units on inventory sites; Chapter 17.40 inclusionary requires 10% of units in rental projects of 35 or more units (7% at 80% AMI low income, 3% at 50% AMI very low income), 55 years, or an in-lieu fee paid to the A-LHTF.
set.next_deadline: Applies at project application; no deadline.
set.cycle_notes: Chapter 18.52 last amended by Ord. 6627 on August 11, 2026. Chapter 17.40 applies to applications submitted on or after October 8, 2024.
set.layering_notes: Anaheim does have a citywide inclusionary ordinance for rental projects: Chapter 17.40 (Ord. 6593, October 29, 2024), cross-referenced in Sec. 18.52.020.020, requires 10% onsite affordable units (7% low, 3% very low income) in rental projects of 35 or more units, with in-lieu fees deposited in the A-LHTF; ownership projects are exempt. No affordable housing fee waiver ordinance was located. The Platinum Triangle and Beach Boulevard specific plans offer density, not money. Density bonus and by-right approval do not by themselves provide public funds. Chapter 18.52 read on the zoneomics mirror; Chapter 17.40 read on the gocodebook mirror (amlegal returns 403).
set.audit_note: Tier 4 spot check November 8, 2026: Chapter 18.52 on the zoneomics mirror contains only Secs. 18.52.010 to 18.52.030; the cited Sec. 18.52.100 affordable parking ratios were not found in this chapter, so that claim was removed. prevailing_wage_trigger false has no cited rule; left as is.

reason: Material: layering_notes said Anaheim has no inclusionary ordinance, but Sec. 18.52.020.020 on the source page requires compliance with Chapter 17.40, which mandates 10% affordable units (7% low, 3% very low) in rental projects of 35 or more units; typical_award_size and affordability_requirement updated and a nonexistent Sec. 18.52.100 parking reference removed.
